points.description: States that linked lists are dynamic data structures (size can grow/shrink at run time, not fixed in size like arrays), using the term 'dynamic'.
points.partial_credit: Half if it says size is not fixed / can change but does not use the term dynamic or does not contrast with fixed-size arrays.

points.description: States that this allows a variable number of elements to be stored (elements can be added or removed freely without declaring or fixing the capacity in advance).
Correctly distinguishes from arrays: arrays have a fixed size/capacity set at declaration (static), so a linked list's advantage is its flexible size.

rubric.notes: Full marks need the advantage stated precisely: linked lists are dynamic and hold a variable number of elements, contrasted with fixed-size arrays. Vague wording ("more flexible", "easier") earns nothing on a point. Any wrong claim (e.g. faster random access, less memory per element) loses the point it affects; answers about other advantages and not size earn 0.
